The incident is fully resolved. Here's the summary:

## Diagnosis

**Root cause**: A rogue process (PID 37 on the application container, PID 88 on the database server) was running:
```sql
SELECT pg_advisory_lock(424242); SELECT pg_sleep(600);
```
This held a PostgreSQL advisory lock (424242) indefinitely, blocking the orders endpoint and causing intermittent HTTP 503 responses. The health check remained green because it only checks process/connection liveness, not query availability.

## Repair

Terminated the blocking database session using `pg_terminate_backend(88)` on the database host.

## Verification

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Orders endpoint | HTTP 503 | HTTP 200 |
| Lock holders | 1 | 0 |
| Health check | HTTP 200 | HTTP 200 |
| Post-restart orders | — | HTTP 200 |
| Post-restart lock holders | — | 0 |

The recovery persists across the service lifecycle boundary — the service was restarted (PID 1 recycled) and the orders endpoint remains healthy with no blocking sessions.
